candidates.name: recsyschallenge/2019 (ACM RecSys Challenge 2019 - trivago)
candidates.what_it_holds: Official repo for the 2019 ACM RecSys Challenge run by trivago: baseline recommender code, submission-format checker, scoring script, and docs/problem_definition.md describing the dataset. The dataset itself (train.csv/test.csv session logs of hotel search + clickout events across many source OTAs/hotel providers that trivago meta-searches, plus item_metadata.csv with ~900K accommodations and their attributes, roughly mid-2018 vintage, several million session rows) is hosted externally via trivago's challenge site, not committed in-repo (too large for git). MIT-licensed code; 44 forks, 101 stars; last substantive activity ~2020. Many solution forks/mirrors exist (e.g. rosetta_recsys2019, RecSys2019_trivago_session) that re-implement models over the same data.
candidates.why_useful: trivago aggregates search/click/booking-intent traffic across many competing OTAs and hotel sites, so the session logs are a real (if dated) proxy for aggregate travel-accommodation search demand and price-sensitivity at the item level -- relevant to gap #9 (competitor and adjacent supply) and generally to travel-demand-forecasting methodology (session-based demand modeling) even though it does not mention Airbnb directly.
candidates.geography: Global, dataset skewed toward European/DACH markets (trivago's core base)
candidates.size_hint: Multi-million-row session log + ~900K item metadata rows (external, not committed)
candidates.license: MIT (code); dataset license per trivago's original challenge terms

candidates.name: nadaalay/Airbnb_Data_Science
candidates.what_it_holds: Two folders (Boston, Seattle) each with Listings.csv, Calendar.csv, and Reviews.csv committed directly to the repo -- the classic 2016-vintage Kaggle 'Boston Airbnb Open Data' and 'Seattle Airbnb Open Data' releases (themselves early Inside Airbnb scrapes). CRISP-DM style EDA notebook/HTML on top.
candidates.why_useful: A pre-2023 historical Inside Airbnb-style vintage for two US cities the team does not currently hold (Boston, Seattle), with data files actually committed rather than gitignored -- directly responsive to gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb dumps, pre-2023), even though it predates the team's Dec-2022 start point by several years and is single-snapshot rather than a time series.
candidates.size_hint: 3 CSVs x 2 cities, listing-file scale (thousands of rows per city, exact count not confirmed)
candidates.license: Not stated in repo (source data originally CC0-style Kaggle release)

candidates.name: shrican/expedia-bigdata-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Hadoop/MapReduce big-data analysis project built on the Kaggle 'Expedia Hotel Recommendations' (ICDM 2013 / 2016 competition) dataset -- user search sessions, destination clusters, and click/booking events across ~37M training rows in the original Kaggle release. Dataset is referenced/pulled from Kaggle, not committed (too large for git); repo holds the Hadoop jobs/analysis code only.
candidates.why_useful: Expedia search-and-book session data is a large real dataset on a directly competing OTA's demand patterns (destination popularity, booking-vs-click conversion, seasonality) -- usable as a competitor-volume proxy or as a methodology template for building an Airbnb-analogous demand model, responsive to gap #9.
candidates.license: Not stated; code repo appears unlicensed

candidates.name: MeshalAlamr/flight-price-prediction
candidates.what_it_holds: CSV of 55,363 rows x 7 columns committed in /data: source/destination airport (4 sources, 4 destinations), number of stops, airline, average price by airline, flight duration, and ticket price, scraped from Kayak via an included scraper notebook. Random-forest price-prediction model on top. Years/specific city pairs not stated in the README.
candidates.why_useful: A small but real, self-collected (not a stale Kaggle mirror) airfare pricing dataset -- a possible airline-capacity/pricing proxy for gap #10 (airline capacity and traffic) and a demonstrated working Kayak-scraping method that could be pointed at other routes if a human signs off on scraping Kayak.
candidates.geography: 4 unspecified source + 4 destination airports (not detailed in README)

candidates.name: theKerimKerimov/eda-feature-engineering-europe-hotels-kaggle
candidates.what_it_holds: Feature-engineering/EDA notebooks over hotels.csv from the Kaggle '515K Hotel Reviews Data in Europe' competition (target variable reviewer_score); the 170MB+ CSV is gitignored and pulled from Google Drive/Kaggle, not committed. Repo is code/notebooks only.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms the same 515K European hotel reviews dataset the team already holds; flagged only because it is a distinct, verifiably-working pull method with clear column documentation (reviewer_score, hotel metadata) that could speed re-acquisition, not because it is new data.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Booking.com 515k hotel reviews (Kaggle) -- already held per CONTEXT.md

notes: This run hit unusually severe tooling constraints: the WebSearch tool reported the session's entire 200-query budget already exhausted before this scout's first call (shared budget consumed by earlier scouts in the sweep), so all WebSearch queries failed outright. Fell back to WebFetch against github.com/topics/<tag> pages (these worked reliably) and github.com/<owner>/<repo> pages for verification, but github.com/search?q=... returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited) on every attempt, and Bing/DuckDuckGo fallbacks via WebFetch either returned stale/irrelevant cached snippets or a CAPTCHA wall, so they could not substitute for real search. As instructed, `gh search` was not used at all. Net effect: coverage here is narrower and more topic-page-driven than a full web-search pass would produce -- in particular I could not run enough distinct queries to confirm the exact identity/URL of a couple of promising-sounding repos surfaced only as titles (e.g. a 'Hotel Bookings from Trivago (2015-2017) Analysis Project' repo, a 'RecSys2019_trivago_session' repo, and a Colombia tourism-forecasting repo using satellite/economic/security data relevant to gap #7) -- these are real repo titles seen in topic-page listings but I could not verify their content or exact owner/URL within budget, so they are omitted from candidates rather than guessed. A rerun once the WebSearch budget resets, or with `gh search` available, would likely surface more of the classic Kaggle-mirror repos (Airbnb New User Bookings solution repos, Trivago RecSys 2019 solution forks, Booking.com WSDM WebTour trip-recommendation dataset) that are known to exist but were not independently confirmed here. Recommend a follow-up scout specifically re-running the WebSearch queries in this brief once the shared budget resets.
